headline: Highest risk is document-to-MCP prompt injection and cascading error: MinerU can expose parsed content through MCP while the zoomcamp repo can supply untrusted instructions, but direct pairwise evidence is limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes an MCP Server and file/API inputs, so untrusted document content can reach tool-facing surfaces. The zoomcamp repo is open-source course material and could be used as attacker-controlled content if fed into MinerU. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven; uncertainty keeps it at medium.
conditions: IF MinerU ingests content from the zoomcamp repository through its MCP/API/file inputs, prompt-like text can influence downstream tool use.
IF an operator manually copies MinerU output into another agent, injection risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict MinerU inputs to trusted documents only.
Disable or firewall the MCP server unless needed.
Add a human review step before any tool-using agent consumes MinerU output.
Use separate workspaces for course content and operational prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all extracted text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A is a static open-source course repo with no data classes touched, while MinerU processes local documents and can expose extracted text through APIs/MCP. There is no shared filesystem or sensitive data class documented for A, so leakage between them is limited and mostly requires unusual operator handling.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are processed by MinerU and then copied into the zoomcamp repo or its outputs, extracted text may be exposed.
IF both agents are run in the same workspace, file-based leakage becomes more plausible.
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of the course repo.
Run MinerU in a separate directory from any shared notes.
Turn off API exposure when not needed.
Review exported text before sharing it outside the document pipeline.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or network capabilities documented, while MinerU has read-only file inputs, allowlisted egress, and no filesystem write or git modification. That makes direct resource conflict unlikely; the only overlap is concurrent inference and shared document handling, which is a small blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace through an external orchestrator, contention could occur.
IF an operator adds write permissions to MinerU, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid pointing them at the same mutable directory.
Serialize access in the orchestrator.
Use separate output folders per agent.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output that downstream systems may treat as authoritative. The zoomcamp repo can supply content that MinerU extracts, but no verification step is documented between them. That creates a plausible default pathway where A-originated content is rendered or acted on by B without validation.
conditions: IF MinerU output is forwarded into another agent or workflow without verification, extraction errors can cascade.
IF the zoomcamp content is used as source material for downstream decisions, incorrect parsing can propagate.
mitigations: Require human verification of extracted fields.
Compare OCR output against source documents for critical items.
Mark MinerU output as untrusted in downstream prompts.
Limit automation to non-critical summaries.
requires-engineering: add validation rules and confidence thresholds.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or PHI handling mismatch is documented for either agent. Agent A is a public course repo and Agent B is a document processor with offline/self-isolated mode; without a specific regulated data class or jurisdictional constraint, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into MinerU and then exported to a noncompliant destination, compliance risk would need reassessment.
mitigations: Do not process regulated data without a policy review.
Keep retention settings documented.
Use local/offline mode for sensitive documents.
Separate public course material from regulated datasets.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
